limits: Fit checks are visual only (straight line on transformed axes); no goodness-of-fit test or tolerance is given.
Python 2 era code and URLs (thinkstats.com data, erf.py, myplot) have dated; math.erf exists since 3.2.
Chapter text states Section 6.6 explains normal ubiquity; not covered here.
Normal model fails in lower tail of birth weight; lognormal fails in upper tail of weights.
practices: Check exponential fit by plotting the CCDF on a log-y scale; a straight line with slope -lambda indicates fit (4.1).
Check Pareto fit by plotting CCDF on log-log axes (4.2).
Use a normal probability plot built from sorted data against sorted standard-normal samples or rankits for normality (4.4).
Test lognormality by checking whether log of the values is normal (4.5).
Choose a model only if it fits the region you care about, e.g. do not use the normal for preterm babies (4.3).
Generate random values from any distribution via inverse CDF on a uniform p (4.7).
